source:
For the first time in my long life I resent my height. 

Never am I untouched. People watch obsessively, one after another and another. They climb the rope ladder and sit on my upper boughs and peer through their handheld distance-lookers at the surrounding landscape. All day, all night. When they see something unfamiliar, they blow on a piercing metal whistle. Then everyone on the ground scurries about like mice. 

I recall, decades ago, I thought the world held order in all its patterns. The birds returned in spring. The insects rest in the fall. The people toil in their various ways and hold their rituals across each year. They all involved me in their patterns. But my height was my own to enjoy. 

Then time gives me clarity: all is disorder. Patterns are illusions. Rituals are delusions. Life is but a violent fight against itself. The only true constant is this:life begets disorder and then life resists disorder, and then life begets disorder… and on and on.     

These years especially, disorder spreads and, with it, blood and sorrow.

在我漫长的一生中，我第一次怨恨自己的高大。

我再也没有不受碰触的时候。人们执着地守望，一个接着一个。他们爬上绳梯，坐在我高处的枝干上，用手里那种看远方的器具，窥看四周的地景。整天，整夜。一看见陌生的东西，就吹响尖锐的金属哨子。接着，地上的所有人便像老鼠般四处奔窜。

我记得，几十年前，我曾以为世界的一切规律都蕴含秩序。鸟儿在春天归来，昆虫在秋天休息。人们以各种方式劳动，每年举行各自的仪式。他们的规律都将我纳入其中。但我的高度，仍属于我自己，任我享受。

后来，时间让我看清：一切都是混乱。规律是幻象，仪式是妄想。生命不过是不断与自身进行的一场暴烈搏斗。唯一真正恒久的，是生命孕育混乱，接着生命抵抗混乱，然后生命又孕育混乱……如此往复不息。

尤其这些年，混乱不断蔓延，鲜血与悲伤也随之扩散。

My favorite memory is from last year during the fall harvist festivul because there was so much good food and games. There was apple and oat bars, hunny pepper deer jerky (my favarite) and a bunch of contests like the sack race and egg toss. It’s the only time of year where everyone shares there things and is happy and the town smells AMAZING. 

My best friend Jill and me came in 3rd place during the three legged race (because we practiced all during spring). Our prize was a bag of maple seerup cookies which we ate in probably 2 seckonds. We even beat two soldiers who fell over during the race! 

Then at night some people got out instramints like a gitar, a pipe, and a harmonika and they made music. The old folks new a bunch of dances so we just watched them and tried to copy their feet. 

Imagine if the fall festivul could happen all the time. If I was the leader in town I would make every day like this. Why can’t we do it now?
